procedure_column: Navarro et al. 2024 (ACS ESC 8) Iron meteorites Spot analysis ns-LA-SF-ICP-MS University of Campinas

Procedure Name.cell: Navarro et al. (2024) Iron Meteorite Spot v1
Procedure Name.value: Navarro et al. (2024) Iron Meteorite Spot v1

Laboratory.cell: Isotope Geology Laboratory, University of Campinas (UNICAMP), Brazil
Laboratory.value: Isotope Geology Laboratory, University of Campinas (UNICAMP), Brazil

Funding Source for Procedure Development.cell: N — the acknowledgements name CNPq grant 316191/2021-3 (J.E.) and support for a conference presentation; neither is for procedure development

Procedure Reference(s).cell: Navarro et al. (2024) ACS Earth Space Chem. 8, 281; Longerich et al. (1996)
Procedure Reference(s).value: Navarro et al. (2024) ACS Earth Space Chem. 8, 281; Longerich et al. (1996)

Sampling Unit Type.cell: Whole sample (polished ~1 cm fragment) > Spot — "fragments about 1 cm were mounted in epoxy resin, polished, and cleaned with ultrapure water" (p.3); the reported quantity is the meteorite's bulk composition for chemical classification (Table 1, p.2)

Sample Preparation Method.cell: Fragments ~1 cm mounted in epoxy resin, polished, cleaned with ultrapure water
Sample Preparation Method.value: Fragments ~1 cm mounted in epoxy resin, polished, cleaned with ultrapure water

Sampling Unit Selection Criteria.cell: Phase targeting, as the stated alternative to rastering — "depending on the specific objectives, spot sampling at specific phases may also fulfill the analytical requirements", against the problem that irons have an "inherent natural inhomogeneity, a result of their lamellar exsolution patterns" (p.2)
Sampling Unit Selection Criteria.value: Phase targeting, as the stated alternative to rastering

Pre-Analysis Imaging and Screening.cell: N — the preparation is stated without an imaging step: "Before analyses, fragments about 1 cm were mounted in epoxy resin, polished, and cleaned with ultrapure water" (p.3). The meteorites' structural classes were known beforehand (Table 1, p.2) but no screening of this material is described

ICP-MS Type.cell: Sector field (SF-ICP-MS) (explicitly stated: "sector field inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometer")
ICP-MS Type.value: Sector field (SF-ICP-MS) (explicitly stated: "sector field inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometer")

Interface Cone Configuration.cell: Ni sampler cone; Ni skimmer cone
Interface Cone Configuration.value: Ni sampler cone; Ni skimmer cone

Detector Configuration.cell: Triple mode — Table 2 'detector range'; 'performed in low-resolution and triple mode detection'

Laser Wavelength and Type.cell: 193 nm ArF excimer; pulse duration 4 ns
Laser Wavelength and Type.value: 193 nm ArF excimer; pulse duration 4 ns

Ablation Duration per Spot.cell: 40 s — '20 s of blank measurement (laser-firing with the shutter closed), followed by 40 s of sample ablation'

Carrier Gas and Flow Rate.cell: He: 0.6 l min⁻¹ (MFC 1) + 0.7 l min⁻¹ (MFC 2) in HelEx II cell; combined with Ar makeup via T-piece near torch
Carrier Gas and Flow Rate.value: He: 0.6 l min⁻¹ (MFC 1) + 0.7 l min⁻¹ (MFC 2) in HelEx II cell; combined with Ar makeup via T-piece near torch

Make-up Gas and Flow Rate.cell: Ar makeup gas, combined via a T-piece near the torch; Table 2 lists a nebulizer gas flow rate of 1.1 L/min — Table 2
Make-up Gas and Flow Rate.value: Ar makeup gas, combined via a T-piece near the torch; Table 2 lists a nebulizer gas flow rate of 1.1 L/min

ICP Tuning.cell: ICP-MS and laser settings optimised daily 'to achieve the compromise between optimum signal intensity and low oxide formation, as specified by the factory'; mass calibration and detector cross-calibration 'systematically checked and redone if required' — Experimental section
ICP Tuning.value: ICP-MS and laser settings optimised daily 'to achieve the compromise between optimum signal intensity and low oxide formation, as specified by the factory'; mass calibration and detector cross-calibration 'systematically checked and redone if required'

Analysis Sequence.cell: 3 × NIST SRM 612 and 3 × North Chile, then blocks of ten unknowns, each followed by 2 × NIST SRM 612 and 2 × North Chile — Experimental section
Analysis Sequence.value: 3 × NIST SRM 612 and 3 × North Chile, then blocks of ten unknowns, each followed by 2 × NIST SRM 612 and 2 × North Chile

Target Species.cell: Cr, Fe, Co, Ni, Cu, Ga, Ge, As, Ru, Rh, Pd, W, Re, Os, Ir, Pt, Au — Table 2

Monitored Masses.key: defines: monitored property per target species
Monitored Masses.cell: ⁵²Cr → Cr; ⁵⁷Fe → Fe; ⁵⁹Co → Co; ⁶¹Ni → Ni; ⁶⁵Cu → Cu; ⁶⁹Ga → Ga; ⁷²Ge → Ge; ⁷⁵As → As; ⁹⁹Ru → Ru; ¹⁰³Rh → Rh; ¹⁰⁵Pd → Pd; ¹⁸²W → W; ¹⁸⁵Re → Re; ¹⁸⁹Os → Os; ¹⁹³Ir → Ir; ¹⁹⁵Pt → Pt; ¹⁹⁷Au → Au — Table 2, with relative abundances; for Fe and Ni the lower-abundance isotopes 'allow their measurement in the analog mode'

Reported Variables and Units.cell: Fe, Ni (g/100 g); Cr, Co, Cu, Ga, Ge, As, Ru, Rh, Pd, W, Re, Os, Ir, Pt, Au (µg/g); chemical classification (nominal) — Table 3 and Table 5

Dwell Time per Mass.cell: all: 0.02 s sample time — E-scan, 100 samples per peak (Table 2)

Background Count Time.cell: 20 s — laser firing with the shutter closed, before each ablation

Number of Replicates.cell: 20 spots in Arraias; n per meteorite in Table 3 — 'the mean value of 20 spot measurements in the Arraias meteorite'
Number of Replicates.value: 20 spots in Arraias; n per meteorite in Table 3

Internal Standard Approach.cell: all: sum normalization, Fe + Ni + Co = 100% — 'In the final step, sum normalization was applied to the major constituents of iron meteorites, specifically Fe + Ni + Co = 100%. This ... eliminated the conventional practice of needing an internal standard'

Internal Standard Element.cell: all: none — Fe + Ni + Co sum normalisation

Blank / Background Correction Method.cell: 20 s blank before each spot, laser firing with the shutter closed; LODs calculated per acquisition in iolite 4 — Experimental section
Blank / Background Correction Method.value: 20 s blank before each spot, laser firing with the shutter closed; LODs calculated per acquisition in iolite 4

Pulse/Analog Detector Nonlinearity Corre.cell: N — 'detector cross-calibration were systematically checked and redone if required'; Fe and Ni measured on low-abundance isotopes in analog mode

Spectral Interference Corrections Applie.cell: No mathematical correction; isotopes chosen to avoid interferences — 'the molecular species 40Ar61Ni interferes severely at mass 101 ... so a better choice is 99Ru, although it is interfered with by the species 40Ar59Co but much less intensely. All used isotopes (Table 2) were chosen based on the above criteria'
Spectral Interference Corrections Applie.value: No mathematical correction; isotopes chosen to avoid interferences

Interfering Species.cell: ⁹⁹Ru: ⁴⁰Ar⁵⁹Co, much less intensely than ⁴⁰Ar⁶¹Ni on ¹⁰¹Ru; other: N — polyatomic ions from Fe and Ni with plasma species are the main concern

value.value: ⁴⁰Ar⁵⁹Co, much less intensely than ⁴⁰Ar⁶¹Ni on ¹⁰¹Ru

Interference Correction Method.cell: ⁹⁹Ru: isotope selection, avoiding ¹⁰¹Ru; other: N — isotopes were chosen to be free of elemental isobaric interference

Normalization / Standards-Based Correcti.cell: all: Fe + Ni + Co = 100% sum normalisation after calibration — the final step of the 3D Trace Elements DRS

value.value: Fe + Ni + Co = 100% sum normalisation after calibration

Analysis Inclusion and Rejection Criteri.cell: Partially — contributing counts are stated ('n: number of replicates'; 'the mean value of 20 spot measurements in the Arraias meteorite'); no acceptance or rejection rule is stated

Combination Method.cell: all: average of n replicate spot measurements per meteorite — 'average (x̅); s: standard deviation of n measured values'; 'the mean value of 20 spot measurements in the Arraias meteorite'

value.value: average of n replicate spot measurements per meteorite

Primary Calibration Standard Name.cell: all [all: NIST SRM 612 and North Chile (Filomena, IIAB)] — median yield correction factors for NIST SRM 612 relative to North Chile, then least-squares calibration per 15 min block, interpolated in time (3D Trace Elements DRS)

value.value: NIST SRM 612 and North Chile (Filomena, IIAB)

Calibration Standard Measurement Frequen.cell: Every ten unknowns (about every 15 min) — calibration blocks bracket blocks of ten unknowns; 'every 15 min calibration block'

Secondary Reference Materials.cell: North Chile — 'also measured as an unknown sample several times, on different days, over four months', for intermediate precision; eight other known iron meteorites validate against published INAA values

Detection Limit.cell: As: 2; Au: 0.1; Co: 2; Cr: 19; Cu: 0.8; Fe: 60; Ga: 0.3; Ge: 3; Ir: 0.2; Ni: 36; Os: 0.2; Pd: 0.5; Pt: 0.3; Re: 0.1; Rh: 0.1; Ru: 1; W: 1 — µg/g, median values (Table 3 'LOD')

Detection Limit Method.cell: all: Longerich et al., calculated for each acquisition in iolite 4 — 'the LOD must be calculated for each acquisition'; Table 3 gives the medians

value.value: Longerich et al., calculated for each acquisition in iolite 4

Counting Statistics Error.key: sample > sampling unit x reported property

Internal (Within-Measurement) Analytical.key: sample > sampling unit x reported property

Within-Session Analytical Precision and.cell: N — precision is stated for samples: RSD <15% for 20 spots in Arraias except Cr (20%), Ir (16%) and Os (20%), and better than 20% for the other meteorites

Between-Session (Long-Term) Analytical P.cell: North Chile [all: RSD 20% at worst] — measured as an unknown over four months; its RSD represents 'the laboratory reproducibility or intermediate precision conditions'

Analytical Accuracy and Assessment Metho.cell: N — assessed on eight known iron meteorites, not a standard: 'More than 75% of published values are within the respective LA-ICP-MS result ±2s'; relative differences 'almost always within ±20%' (Fig. 2)

Additional Notes.cell: Two measurement standards complement each other: North Chile for matrix similarity and NIST SRM 612 for its well-known composition; Fe + Ni + Co = 100% normalisation removes the need for an internal standard
Additional Notes.value: Two measurement standards complement each other: North Chile for matrix similarity and NIST SRM 612 for its well-known composition; Fe + Ni + Co = 100% normalisation removes the need for an internal standard
